title: Filter silently blocks all bundles
problem: A Make filter between two modules has a condition that evaluates to false for all bundles passing through. The scenario executes without error but produces no output downstream — a silent failure.
symptoms: Scenario runs successfully (green checkmark) but no data is processed downstream
Module after the filter shows 0 bundles processed
No error message is generated — the scenario appears healthy
Target system shows no new records after execution

likely_causes.cause: Filter condition compares values of different types (e.g., string '1' vs number 1)
Filter is case-sensitive and the source value casing does not match the hardcoded comparison value
The field used in the filter condition is absent or null in all current bundles
The external API changed the value or format of the filtered field
Filter references a variable that is empty or undefined at runtime

diagnosis_steps: Run the scenario with 'Run once' and inspect bundle output before the filter
Note the exact value and type (string, number, boolean) of the field used in the filter
Compare with the filter condition: are the types identical? Is the casing identical?
Temporarily set the filter option to allow bundles through when the condition does not match to see what would pass through
Add a Tools > Set Variables module before the filter to normalize the value (e.g., lower(), toString()) and inspect the result

solutions.solution: Use the lower() function on string comparisons to neutralize case sensitivity: {{lower(1.status)}} = active
solutions.conditions: When the filter fails due to case mismatch on a string field

solutions.solution: Use toString() or toNumber() to ensure type consistency before comparison
solutions.conditions: When the filter fails due to a type mismatch (e.g., string '1' vs number 1)

solutions.solution: Add an 'Exists' condition on the filtered field in addition to the value condition to handle null or absent fields
solutions.conditions: When the filtered field can be absent or null in some bundles

solutions.solution: Add a parallel Router branch with the inverted filter condition and route rejected bundles to a logger or notification during debugging
solutions.conditions: During debugging to observe exactly what is being rejected and why

prevention: Always test filters using 'Run once' with real data before deploying
Normalize string values (lower(), trim()) in a Set Variables module before filtering on them
Add a diagnostic inverted-filter branch during development to log rejected bundles

origin_details.evidence: Filter behavior is well-documented in Make Help Center. The silent nature of filter rejection (no error thrown) is confirmed conceptually by Make's architecture. Specific case-sensitivity behavior of string comparisons was inferred from Make's general string handling — not found as explicit statement in official docs.

audit_notes: Filter behavior is well-documented in Make Help Center. The silent nature of filter rejection (no error thrown) is confirmed conceptually by Make's architecture. Specific case-sensitivity behavior of string comparisons was inferred from Make's general string handling — not found as explicit statement in official docs.

title: Filter AND/OR logic produces unexpected results
problem: A Make filter with multiple conditions using AND/OR logic does not evaluate as the user expects. The confusion commonly arises because Make filters conditions within a single filter block as AND, while multiple filter blocks in sequence are evaluated as OR.
symptoms: Filter passes bundles that should have been blocked, or blocks bundles that should have passed
Scenario logic is incorrect but no error is thrown
Adding more conditions to a filter does not have the expected narrowing effect

likely_causes.cause: Multiple conditions within a single filter block are evaluated as AND — the user expected OR
Multiple filter blocks in sequence are evaluated as OR — the user expected AND

diagnosis_steps: Open the filter and count the number of condition blocks and conditions within each block
Determine whether the intended logic requires AND (all must match) or OR (any must match)
For AND: put all conditions in a single filter block. For OR: use multiple filter blocks or a Router with one condition per route

solutions.solution: To require ALL conditions to match (AND): place all conditions within a single filter block using the '+' button to add conditions within the same block
solutions.conditions: When all conditions must be true simultaneously

solutions.solution: To require ANY condition to match (OR): use multiple filter blocks (each containing one condition) or use a Router with one route per condition, each converging to the same downstream modules
solutions.conditions: When any one of several conditions being true is sufficient to pass the bundle

prevention: Before building a filter, explicitly define the intended logic: 'all of these must match' (AND) or 'any of these must match' (OR)
Test filters with at least 3 types of records: one that should pass all conditions, one that fails one condition, and one that fails all conditions

origin_details.evidence: Make documentation describes the AND/OR behavior of conditions within and between filter blocks.

evidence.claim: In Make, multiple conditions within a single filter block are evaluated as AND; multiple filter blocks are evaluated as OR

sequence: wrong bundles pass or are blocked
conditions: Multiple conditions with misunderstood AND/OR semantics

diagnostic_signals: Filter is passing bundles that should fail, or blocking bundles that should pass
Filter has multiple conditions — AND/OR logic may be misunderstood
Scenario produces wrong output with no error
audit_notes: AND/OR behavior within and between filter blocks is documented in Make Help Center. The specific UI description ('+' button for same-block conditions) is consistent with Make's filter interface.

title: Filter numeric comparison fails due to string vs number type
problem: A filter condition comparing a numeric field uses '=' or '>=' but always evaluates as false because the field value is stored as Text (string) rather than Number. String '10' is not equal to and not greater than number 5 in Make's typed comparison.
symptoms: A numeric filter condition never passes any bundles even when values appear correct
Bundles with a value of '10' fail a '> 5' condition when '10' is stored as text
Filter works in some scenarios but not others — the difference is the source type

likely_causes.cause: The filtered field is returned as a Text (string) type by the source module, not as a Number type — string comparison is different from numeric comparison
The comparison value in the filter is entered as a string instead of a number

diagnosis_steps: Inspect the field type in the bundle inspector — confirm whether it is tagged as 'Number' or 'Text'
If it is 'Text', add a parseNumber() or toNumber() conversion in a Set Variables module before the filter
Alternatively, use a text-based comparison operator in the filter if converting to number is not possible

solutions.solution: Add a Set Variables module before the filter to convert the string field to a number: {{parseNumber(1.amount; '.')}} then filter on the converted variable
solutions.conditions: When the source field is a string representation of a number

solutions.solution: Use a text comparison operator if numeric comparison is not required — note that text comparison of numbers can produce unexpected ordering ('10' < '9' as text)
solutions.conditions: When conversion is not possible and approximate behavior is acceptable

prevention: Always check the field type before building numeric filter conditions
Apply parseNumber() conversion in a Set Variables module immediately after the source module for any field that will be used in numeric comparisons
search_keywords: make filter greater than not working

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Filters and Data types
origin_details.evidence: Make filter conditions are type-aware. Numeric comparisons require Number type fields.

evidence.claim: Make filter conditions are type-sensitive — a numeric comparison requires the field to be of Number type, not Text
Make's parseNumber() converts string numbers to Number type

diagnostic_signals: Filter numeric condition never passes any bundle
Bundle inspector shows type 'Text' on the filtered field
Filter works after adding parseNumber() conversion
audit_notes: Type-sensitive filter behavior inferred from Make's data type system and confirmed in community. The specific claim about string vs numeric comparison behavior is consistent with Make's typed evaluation model.

title: Filter date comparison produces unexpected results
problem: A filter comparing a date field to a value (before today, after a date, etc.) does not work correctly because the date field is stored as Text rather than as a Make Date type, or the comparison date is not formatted correctly.
symptoms: Date-based filter condition passes or blocks all bundles regardless of the date value
A 'before today' condition is always true or always false
Date comparison works for some records but fails for others due to inconsistent date formats

likely_causes.cause: The date field is typed as Text in the bundle — date string comparison does not behave like calendar date comparison
The comparison value in the filter uses a format that does not match Make's Date type expectations

diagnosis_steps: Check the date field type in the bundle inspector — confirm it is 'Date' not 'Text'
If it is 'Text', use parseDate() to convert it to a Make Date type before the filter
Use the now function or a specific date in Make's supported format for the comparison value

solutions.solution: Add parseDate(1.date_field; 'YYYY-MM-DD') in a Set Variables module before the filter to convert the text date to a Make Date type
solutions.conditions: When the date field is stored as Text

solutions.solution: Use {{now}} as the comparison value in a 'Date is after' or 'Date is before' filter condition when filtering relative to the current date
solutions.conditions: When filtering records by their date relative to today

prevention: Always verify date field types before building date-based filter conditions
Use parseDate() to normalize date values from external sources before filtering

origin_details.evidence: parseDate() is documented in Make. Date type vs Text type distinction is fundamental to Make's data model.

evidence.claim: Make's parseDate() converts a date string to a Date type for use in date-sensitive comparisons
Make provides the 'now' variable for use in date comparisons within filters

sequence: source returns date as text string
filter date comparison on text type
conditions: Filter expects Date type for calendar comparison

diagnostic_signals: Date filter passes or blocks all bundles regardless of the date value
Bundle inspector shows 'Text' type on a date field used in filter
Filter works after adding parseDate() conversion
audit_notes: parseDate() and now confirmed in Make documentation. Type-sensitive date filter behavior consistent with Make's typed data model.

title: Using 'Exists' condition to handle optional or absent fields
problem: A filter condition comparing a field value with a specific value fails when the field is absent from some bundles — the comparison evaluates differently than expected for absent fields. The correct approach is to first check field existence using the 'Exists' condition operator.
symptoms: A filter blocks records where an optional field is absent, even when absent means 'should pass'
A filter passes records where a required field is absent, which should have been blocked
Inconsistent filtering behavior for records with different field presence

likely_causes.cause: The filter condition assumes the field always exists — records without the field behave unexpectedly under value-comparison conditions
The 'Exists' operator is not used to gate the value comparison when the field is optional

diagnosis_steps: Identify which fields in the filter condition are optional in the source data
For each optional field, add an 'Exists' condition check before or alongside the value comparison
Test the filter with records that have the field present, absent, and with an explicit null value

solutions.solution: Add an 'Exists' filter condition on optional fields before comparing their values. In the same filter block, add 'field' 'Exists' as the first condition and the value comparison as the second — both must be true (AND logic).
solutions.conditions: When a field is optional and should only be compared when it exists

solutions.solution: Use the 'Does not exist' condition to route or filter out records where a required field is absent
solutions.conditions: When records missing a required field should be explicitly handled or skipped

prevention: For every filter condition, ask: 'Can this field be absent?' If yes, add an Exists check
Test filters with edge-case records: field present, field absent, field present with null value

origin_details.evidence: Make provides 'Exists' and 'Does not exist' filter operators for handling optional fields.

evidence.claim: Make filters include 'Exists' and 'Does not exist' operators for checking field presence

sequence: some bundles have field, some do not
filter evaluates value comparison on absent field
conditions: Optional field not checked with Exists before value comparison

diagnostic_signals: Filter behaves inconsistently — works for some records, not others
Failing records have an absent or null field used in the filter condition
Adding an Exists check fixes the behavior
audit_notes: Exists operator confirmed in Make filter documentation. The evaluation behavior for absent fields is consistent with Make's data model.
